title: Castlevania
wiki_lead:
Castlevania (), known in Japan as Akumajō Dracula, is a gothic horror action-adventure video game series and media franchise created by Konami. The series is largely set in the castle of Count Dracula, the arch-enemy of the Belmont clan of vampire hunters.
Debuting with the 1986 video game on Nintendo's Famicom Disk System, the first entry and the majority of its sequels are side-scrolling action platformers. The 1997 game, Castlevania: Symphony of the Night, originally released for the PlayStation, returned to the nonlinear gameplay first seen in Castlevania II: Simon's Quest, which also introduced role-playing elements and exploration. Several installments later adopted Symphony of the Night's gameplay, which along with Super Metroid, have popularized the Metroidvania genre. 2010 saw the release of Castlevania: Lords of Shadow, a 3D action-adventure game developed by MercurySteam and Kojima Productions that served as a reboot of the series.
The Castlevania series has been released on various platforms; from early systems to modern consoles, as well as handheld devices such as mobile phones. The franchise has since expanded into several spin-off video games and other media; including comic books and a critically acclaimed animated television series.
Spanning four decades, Castlevania is one of Konami's most successful franchises. Retrospectives have attributed the series's success to its blend of action, adventure, and horror elements; and it has been praised for its challenging gameplay mechanics, atmospheric settings, and music.

Games

Most Castlevania titles have been released in Japan, North America, Europe and Australia on various video game consoles, personal computers (PC) and mobile phones, with additional remakes and re-releases.
The first console title, Castlevania, was released on the Famicom Disk System in 1986 and in North America in 1987 on the Nintendo Entertainment System (NES). A 2D sidescrolling action game where the player progresses through six stages, many principal features of the Castlevania series originated with it. It has been ported to many platforms, such as the NES Classic Edition. Also released in 1986 was Vampire Killer for the MSX home computer, which played significantly differently from the original Castlevania, where players had to search for the exit before they could proceed to the next stage. Following that year, in 1987, Castlevania II: Simon's Quest further departed from the standard platforming genre of the first Castlevania for a game more similar to the nonlinear gameplay of Metroid, with several role-playing elements such as a world map which the player is free to explore and revisit.
Haunted Castle (1988), the first arcade title, returned to the linear platforming gameplay of the original. This continued with the first handheld Game Boy entry, Castlevania: The Adventure and the NES sequel, Castlevania III: Dracula's Curse, both released in 1989. grok_lead: Castlevania is a long-running action-adventure video game series developed and published by Konami, renowned for its gothic horror themes and vampire-slaying protagonists. Debuting in Japan on September 26, 1986, for the Family Computer Disk System as AkumajÅ Dracula, the franchise centers on the Belmont clanâa lineage of vampire hunters wielding the legendary Vampire Killer whipâas they confront the recurring threat of Count Dracula, the immortal lord of darkness, and his monstrous forces within labyrinthine castles. The series' gameplay evolved from linear platforming in its early entries, such as the original Castlevania (1986) where players control Simon Belmont navigating trap-filled stages and battling bosses inspired by Universal Monsters, to the nonlinear "Metroidvania" style pioneered by Super Metroid (1994) and Castlevania: Symphony of the Night (1997), the latter featuring Alucard as the protagonist and emphasizing exploration, RPG elements, and ability upgrades in a vast, interconnected world. Key characters include protagonists from the recurring Belmont clan of vampire hunters, with various male descendants serving as primary heroes across the series, beginning chronologically with Leon Belmont in Castlevania: Lament of Innocence (2003), set in 1094; for example, Trevor Belmont is playable in Castlevania III: Dracula's Curse (1989), set in 1476, which introduces allies such as AlucardâDracula's dhampir sonâand the series antagonist Dracula, whose resurrections drive the cyclical narrative across centuries, though Trevor appears in only a limited number of games overall. Over nearly four decades, Castlevania has released over 30 mainline and spin-off titles across platforms from NES to modern consoles and mobile, with notable innovations including 3D explorations in Castlevania: Legacy of Darkness (1999) and multiplayer co-op in Castlevania: Harmony of Despair (2010). The franchise's influence extends beyond games, inspiring animated Netflix series (2017âpresent) that adapt its lore into a darker, more narrative-driven format, while collections like the Castlevania Anniversary Collection (2019) and Castlevania Dominus Collection (2024) preserve its classics for new generations. In February 2026, Konami announced Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, developed in collaboration with the teams behind Dead Cells and The Rogue Prince of Persia, a new 2D action-exploration game set for release in 2026 on platforms including PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch, Xbox Series X/S, and PC. Its blend of challenging combat, orchestral soundtracks, and horror aesthetics has cemented Castlevania as a cornerstone of gaming history, selling millions and earning critical acclaim for atmospheric design.
